repairs.currentText: Strongest feature: Oppy clearly defines an inclusively pluralistic natural reality encompassing physical, chemical, biological, and psychological domains, accurately preventing his scientific naturalism from being mistaken for reductive, physics-only metaphysics. Principal limitation: This ontological enumeration demonstrates breadth without establishing why these categories form a unified natural reality, whether they possess relevant explanatory irreducibility, or why their collective framework compares favorably with Kastrup’s consciousness-first alternative. Live burden: Oppy must provide a noncircular criterion distinguishing the natural from whatever happens to exist, explain how these plural descriptive vocabularies coexist coherently, and reconcile their apparent autonomy with his subsequent identification of mental processes and environmentally embedded neural processes. Locked score: The locked score of 81 recognizes an accurate, relevant, charitable, and strategically clarifying definition of the con position, while appropriately withholding stronger credit because evidential justification, ontological unification, and comparative argumentative leverage remain substantially undeveloped.
repairs.lockedDescription: Because natural reality includes physical, chemical, biological, and psychological domains, Oppy concludes that scientific naturalism need not collapse every explanation into physics.

repairs.currentText: Strongest feature: Oppy lucidly contrasts mentality as reality’s fundamental basis with minds and ideas as historically late, locally situated developments, thereby giving the metaphysical disagreement a clear and directly motion-relevant structure. Principal limitation: An empirical chronology may establish when organisms displaying mentality emerged, but this move supplies no sufficient bridge from their temporal appearance to the stronger ontological conclusion that subjectivity itself cannot be fundamental. Live burden: Oppy must address analytic idealism’s distinction between individual minds and transpersonal subjectivity, because Kastrup can consistently accept that personal minds arose late in natural history while denying that experience as such originated alongside them. Locked score: The locked score of 79 rewards the contrast’s coherence, relevance, lucidity, and economical framing, while recognizing that its warrant remains compressed and its generic characterization of idealism does not adequately capture the specific explanatory architecture of Kastrup’s position.
repairs.lockedDescription: Because minds appear late and locally in natural history, Oppy contrasts scientific naturalism with idealism’s claim that mentality is fundamental to reality.
